# Local polygonization with arbitrary Jensen contact sets in the independent case

This is a strengthening of the stable-contact local Gram construction. It
requires linear independence of the residual support functions, but no
stable equality pattern or positive gap in the support compatibility
constraints. Contact sets may be arbitrary closed sets.

## Theorem

Let finitely many positive planar fibers K_z satisfy all their finite-base
Jensen support inequalities. On a closed normal interval I=[a,b] of length
less than pi, suppose every h_z is C2 on a neighborhood and every curvature
radius h_z''+h_z has a uniform positive lower bound. Let B_z solve
B_z''+B_z=0 with the same endpoint support values, and put f_z=h_z-B_z.
Assume the functions {f_z} are linearly independent.

Suppose each of finitely many prescribed ambient caps has constant strict
membership on each of these compact fiber arcs. Then all arcs admit
simultaneous arbitrarily close polygonal replacements preserving every
fiber area, every specified cap area, the outside supports, and ALL Jensen
support inequalities exactly. No regularity assumption is made on the
contact sets of those inequalities.

## Proof

Use the interval energy Q(f,g)=integral(f'g'-fg), which is positive definite
on H_0^1(I). Take a sufficiently fine uniform common mesh of spacing delta,
and let P denote nodal piecewise-sin/cos interpolation. The proof in
`candidate 37af539d763eaa93` shows P is Q-orthogonal
projection. Put F_z=P f_z and

    G_zw=Q(F_z,F_w),
    d_z=(1/2)Q(f_z-F_z,f_z-F_z).

The matrix G is positive definite for fine meshes, with inverse uniformly
bounded; d=O(delta^2). The initial circumscribed polygonal support
h_z^mesh=B_z+F_z has area excess exactly d_z.

Unlike a general Gram restoration, use ONE common additive correction

    psi=sum_w xi_w F_w,
    new h_z=h_z^mesh+psi        for every z.               (1)

Its fiber-area increment is

    -Q(F_z,psi)-(1/2)Q(psi,psi)
       =-(G xi)_z-(1/2)xi^T G xi.

Thus exact area correction is the finite system

    G xi+q 1=d,       q=(1/2)xi^T G xi.                   (2)

For completeness this system has an explicit small solution. Write

    A=1^T G^(-1)1>0,
    B=1^T G^(-1)d=O(delta^2),
    C=d^T G^(-1)d=O(delta^4).

For small delta the discriminant D=(1+B)^2-A C is positive. Set

    q=C/[(1+B)+sqrt(D)],
    xi=G^(-1)(d-q 1).

Then q=O(delta^4), xi=O(delta^2), and direct substitution in
Aq^2-2(1+B)q+C=0 proves (2). If d=0, take q=xi=0. Hence every fiber area
is preserved exactly.

The same curvature estimates as in the Gram proof apply. The initial
interior polygon atoms are at least 2c tan(delta/2), while the common
correction changes them by O(delta^3). At the interval endpoints the
initial added atoms are at least c tan(delta/2), while their corrections
are O(delta^2). All curvature atoms remain nonnegative, and the outside
supports are unchanged because every F_z vanishes at a,b. Therefore (1)
defines actual convex bodies with polygonal arcs, arbitrarily close to the
originals.

It remains to prove compatibility WITHOUT any gap assumption. On each
mesh cell [theta_j,theta_(j+1)], a Jensen difference of the interpolated
supports is

    sin(theta_(j+1)-theta)/sin(delta) times its old left-node value
      +sin(theta-theta_j)/sin(delta) times its old right-node value.

Both coefficients and both node values are nonnegative. Thus common-normal
interpolation preserves every Jensen support inequality. In (1), the SAME
psi is then added to each fiber. In a Jensen inequality

    h_z >= sum_w p_w h_w,       sum_w p_w=1,

the correction cancels exactly. Every inequality therefore remains valid,
regardless of where its contact set lies. This works for every barycentric
representation, without selecting only finitely many active inequalities.

Finally, sufficiently close changed regions keep their fixed cap memberships.
Each cap-area change in each fiber is either zero or the full fiber-area
change, which has already been made zero. This proves the theorem.

## Why independence is a real condition for this mechanism

The Jacobian in (2) is the Gram matrix of the residual functions. When they
are dependent, it is singular. A common correction can then genuinely fail:
if f_2=2f_1 and their projection errors satisfy e_2=2e_1 with ||e_1||_Q>0,
restoring both norms by one common psi would require

    2<F_1,psi>+||psi||^2=||e_1||^2,
    4<F_1,psi>+||psi||^2=4||e_1||^2.

Subtract twice the first equation from the second to obtain

    -||psi||^2=2||e_1||^2,

which is impossible. This does not obstruct the separate homothetic-arc
construction, which uses different scaled corrections. The present theorem
is specifically the full-rank common-correction mechanism.
